claims.claim: Michael Dirda opens his review by quoting the first sentence of A Wizard of Earthsea, which names the island of Gont, its mile-high peak, its towns in high valleys and its ports on dark narrow bays before naming any person.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, "The Twilight of an Age of Magic" (review of Tehanu), The Washington Post, 25 February 1990
claims.quote: a single mountain that lifts its peak a mile above
claims.page: review opening, quoting A Wizard of Earthsea

claims.claim: Gerald Jonas, in the New York Times obituary, describes Le Guin’s fiction as combining compelling stories and rigorous narrative logic with a lean but lyrical style.
claims.source: Gerald Jonas, obituary of Ursula K. Le Guin, The New York Times, 23 January 2018

claims.claim: Gerald Jonas states that the first three Earthsea books, written for young adults at the publisher’s request, show no trace of writing down to their audience in scale or style.
claims.source: Gerald Jonas, obituary of Ursula K. Le Guin, The New York Times, 23 January 2018
claims.quote: elevated style betray no trace of writing down to an audience

claims.claim: Le Guin, quoted in her New York Times obituary, said she must find the right name for a character before she can get on with the story.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, quoted by Gerald Jonas, The New York Times obituary, 23 January 2018
claims.quote: I must find the right name or I cannot get on
claims.page: obituary body, paragraph on true names

claims.claim: Sean Guynes states that the tone of Le Guin’s writing in A Wizard of Earthsea is simpler and sparser than in The Left Hand of Darkness or The Dispossessed.
claims.source: Sean Guynes, "A Wizard of Earthsea: The Unsung Song of the Shadow", The Ursula K. Le Guin Reread, Tor.com, 8 April 2020
claims.quote: simpler and sparser than in The Left Hand of Darkness
claims.page: opening section of the reread instalment

claims.claim: Sylvia Kelso states that Le Guin, like Yeats, seems to move toward simplicity or at least austerity in the rhythm and content of her later work.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, "Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin", Paradoxa 21 (2009), pp. 7-22
claims.quote: Le Guin does seem to move toward simplicity

claims.claim: Sylvia Kelso states that Tehanu shows the skill of experience making less do more rather than more do more.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, "Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin", Paradoxa 21 (2009), pp. 7-22
claims.quote: making less do more, rather than more do more

claims.claim: The frame narrator of 'The Matter of Seggri' opens the story in the past tense with a dated archival event rather than a scene.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: The first recorded contact with Seggri was in year 242

claims.claim: The Seggri frame records the killing of an observer by naming exactly what the record does not contain.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: disclosed the fact, but not the circumstances

claims.claim: The Seggri frame marks a gap in the archive with a present-tense statement that no record exists.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: There is no record of further contact with Seggri until
claims.page: frame passage after Captain Aolao-olao's report

claims.claim: The Seggri compiler uses a first-person-plural editorial voice that states the limit of its holding before excerpting a document.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: We have only her report, from which three excerpts follow.

claims.claim: A policy decision in the Seggri frame is reported as an agentless passive with the number written out in words.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: A limit of two hundred visitors from off world was set.

claims.claim: Each document in 'The Matter of Seggri' is introduced by a provenance line naming the kind of document, its recipient and its date.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: The following is a memoir given to Ambassador Eritho te Ves
claims.page: frame line before the Ush memoir

claims.claim: An observer's institutional advice is compressed in the Seggri frame into a nominalisation and two bare verbs.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: Her recommendation was to observe and avoid.

claims.claim: The Seggri frame reports a demographic figure in the present tense as a hedged ratio, giving the balance as about 12:1.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: the gender balance now stands at about 12:1

verdicts.trueWording: Review opens: "THE ISLAND of Gont," begins A Wizard of Earthsea
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (20170827235846id_) of the WaPo archive page; live URL died mid-stream (curl 92). Dirda's review body does open with the novel's opening quotation, and no person is named before Sparrowhawk four sentences in. The quote fragment is verbatim. But the towns/ports detail belongs to the novel's SECOND sentence, which Dirda quotes next, not to the first sentence the claim attributes it to. Byline 'By Michael Dirda', February 25, 1990, reviewing Tehanu - all confirmed.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the claim attributes the towns-in-high-valleys and ports-on-dark-narrow-bays detail to the first sentence; on the page those words fall in the novel's second sentence

verdicts.trueWording: combine compelling stories, rigorous narrative logic and a lean but lyrical style
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (20260111213522id_); live nytimes.com returned HTTP 403. Byline 'By Gerald Jonas', Jan. 23, 2018 confirmed on the capture. Quote 'a lean but lyrical style' appears word for word, and all three combined elements are named in the same sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: their grand scale and elevated style betray no trace of writing down
verdicts.note: Same NYT Wayback capture. Quote verbatim. Every limb holds: 'The first three Earthsea books ... were written, at the request of her publisher, for young adults' and the scale/style clause carries the no-writing-down assertion.

verdicts.trueWording: I must find the right name or I cannot get on
verdicts.note: Same NYT Wayback capture. Quote verbatim inside a direct quotation attributed to Le Guin; the surrounding sentence establishes the 'for a character' limb ('took this discipline seriously in naming her own characters').

verdicts.trueWording: simpler and sparser than in The Left Hand of Darkness
verdicts.note: Live reactormag.com fetched raw (HTTP 200). Byline 'By Sean Guynes', published April 8, 2020, 'The Ursula K. Le Guin Reread', instalment covering A Wizard of Earthsea. Quote verbatim; the sentence names both comparison novels and its subject is A Wizard of Earthsea. Locator note: the sentence sits in the fourth body paragraph, an assessment paragraph near the top, consistent with the claim's 'opening section' hint.

verdicts.trueWording: Le Guin does seem to move toward simplicity, or at least austerity
verdicts.note: PDF fetched raw (HTTP 200) and text-extracted with pdftotext -layout. Article header confirms 'Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin', Sylvia A. Kelso. Quote verbatim, on printed page 16 (running head '16  Sylvia A. Kelso') as cited. The Yeats comparison, simplicity/austerity pair and rhythm-and-content limb are all in the one sentence. Citation nit outside the claim sentence: the PDF masthead reads 'Paradoxa, No. 21, 2008', not 2009.

verdicts.trueWording: Tehanu can show the skill of experience making less do more
verdicts.note: Same Kelso PDF, printed page 16. Quote 'making less do more, rather than more do more' verbatim. One nuance: the page hedges with the modal 'can show'; the claim asserts 'shows'. The substance is supported, so the limb stands, but the modal is softer on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: The first recorded contact with Seggri was in year 242
verdicts.note: sfsfss.com transcription fetched raw (HTTP 200, 95KB). The quoted words are the story's first line of text after title and byline, so the 'opens the story' limb holds. Past tense ('was'), dated archival event ('year 242 of Hainish Cycle 93'), and it is summary frame narration, not a dramatised scene.

verdicts.trueWording: disclosed the fact, but not the circumstances
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Full sentence: 'Kaza Agad had been killed; the Lords of Awaga Castle finally disclosed the fact, but not the circumstances.' Kaza Agad is identified earlier as one of the First Observers, so the 'observer' limb holds. Nuance: the withholding agent on the page is the Lords of Awaga Castle rather than the archive, but the frame's record is thereby left without the circumstances, which is what the claim asserts.

verdicts.trueWording: There is no record of further contact with Seggri until
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim, in the present tense ('There is'), and it directly follows the account of the log being dispersed and preserved only in fragmentary form - so it does mark an archival gap, and it sits where the claim says, after Captain Aolao-olao's report.

verdicts.trueWording: We have only her report, from which three excerpts follow.
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim, first-person-plural 'We', stating the holding's limit ('only her report'), immediately before the excerpted document. Checked the count: exactly three dated excerpts follow (34/223, 34/245, 34/266).

verdicts.trueWording: A limit of two hundred visitors from off world was set.
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim. Agentless passive confirmed - 'was set' with no by-phrase - and the quantity is spelled out in words, not digits. It reports a policy decision following Resehavanar's Choice.

verdicts.trueWording: The following is a short story -written in 93/1586 by
verdicts.note: Same raw page. The cited quotation is verbatim and that one provenance line does name kind, recipient and date. But the claim is universal ('Each document'), and it fails on the other documents. Enumerated all five: Captain Aolao-olao's report (kind and date, no recipient); Merriment's notes (kind, recipient 'THE EKUMEN', date 93/133 - fits); the Ush memoir (fits); Sem Gridji's short story (kind, date, author, NO recipient); Mobile Ardar Dez's autobiographical sketch (kind only, no recipient and no date in its intro line).
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the universal limb that every document's provenance line names a recipient and a date - the short story intro names no recipient, and the autobiographical sketch intro names neither recipient nor date

verdicts.trueWording: Her recommendation was to observe and avoid.
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim. 'Her' is Mobile/First Observer Merriment, and the advice is institutional - the following sentence has the Stabiles overriding it. The nominalisation ('recommendation') plus two bare verbs ('observe', 'avoid') is directly checkable against the quoted words.

verdicts.trueWording: the gender balance now stands at about 12:1
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim, in frame narration. Present tense ('stands'), hedged ('about'), expressed as a ratio, and the figure is 12:1 as claimed.
